headline: TTWO surges nearly 5% on GTA VI hype while PLS gets smacked 4.7% today — US markets were strong last night with NASDAQ up 1.9%.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara got hit hard today, dropping 4.7% to close at $5.88. Lithium stocks have had a strong 2026 overall on AI data centre battery demand, but PLS has been giving back recent gains as the lithium spot price remains volatile. No specific company news today — this looks like broader sector profit-taking after a decent run-up.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a big night last session, up nearly 5% to $239.28 USD. The GTA VI hype machine is running hot — reports are circulating about a potential $80 price tag, a third trailer dropping when pre-orders open, and streamers offering $250K for early access. The market is pricing in a monster launch. This is TTWO's core catalyst right now.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google had a solid session last night, up 1.48% to $367.46 USD. The broader NASDAQ surged 1.91% which lifted all tech boats. No specific Google news drove the move — this was a rising tide lifting a well-positioned ship. Your GOOG position is now up 19.5% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets dipped 0.74% today to $94.44. The ASX broadly fell 0.92%, which dragged this one along. Gold fell overnight which can weigh on commodity-heavy emerging market economies. Nothing dramatic — just a soft day on the local market.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.56% today to $76.83. The ASX 200 fell nearly 1% today, pulling down the Australian portion of this diversified fund. Your overall position is still in the green (+1.93%), so no drama here.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.61% today to $8.10. Crude oil was essentially flat last night (down just 0.08% to $76.54 USD/barrel), so this was more about general ASX weakness than any energy-specific news. US-Iran nuclear talks remain on the radar — an agreement could put downward pressure on oil prices, which would hurt this ETF.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.22% today to $18.16 — a quiet but positive session given the ASX broadly fell. AI regulatory debate is heating up globally (more below), but for now the market isn't spooked. Your position is still slightly underwater overall (-3.85%).

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft barely moved last session, up just 0.13% to $379.40 USD. A Seeking Alpha piece flagged concerns that MSFT isn't cheap and could fall to multi-year lows — the stock's AI strategy is strong but the valuation is stretched. Your MSFT position remains underwater (-14.4%), so this is one to keep an eye on.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS barely moved today, up just 0.07% to $525.46. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, and while the US had a strong night last session (S&P up 1.08%), the ASX-listed version didn't fully reflect that yet — it'll catch up when US sentiment flows through. Your position is up 1.89% overall.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — sharp 4.7% drop today
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals closed at $5.88, down 4.7% in a single session. That pushes your overall loss on PLS to -12.76%. There's no specific bad news today, but the lithium sector is volatile and PLS has been underperforming its peers. If you believe in the AI data centre battery demand story long-term, this could be a hold — but if you're losing conviction, worth reviewing your position size.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI hype is very real
watch_today.detail: Take-Two jumped nearly 5% last session to $239.28, putting your position up 4.33% overall. Pre-launch buzz is intense — an $80 price tag, a third trailer, and streamers paying $250K for early access are all circulating. The launch catalyst is approaching fast. If you were thinking of adding, the risk/reward is getting tighter at this price — hold what you have and let the launch play out.

watch_today.title: MSFT — bearish analysis circulating, still underwater
watch_today.detail: A Seeking Alpha analysis published this weekend argues Microsoft is overvalued and could drop to multi-year lows (lows not seen in several years). Your MSFT position is already down 14.4% (-$57.38 AUD). The stock barely moved last session (+0.13%). Worth watching whether this narrative gains traction — Microsoft's AI spend is high and the market wants to see it translate to earnings growth.

watch_today.title: ASX had a rough day — down 0.92%
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 fell 82 points to close at 8,828 today. Most of your Aussie-listed ETFs (VDHG, VGE, FUEL) felt it. No single dramatic catalyst — general risk-off tone on the local market. US markets were strong last night though, so watch for a potential ASX bounce tomorrow if Wall Street stays positive when it opens tonight.

watch_today.title: US-Iran talks: watch the oil price
watch_today.detail: Reports indicate US-Iran nuclear negotiations are continuing. If a deal is struck, Iran could lift oil exports significantly, pushing crude prices lower. That's a headwind for your FUEL.AX (global energy ETF). Oil is holding around $76.54 USD/barrel for now — relatively stable — but this is worth keeping on the radar this week.

watch_today.title: GOOG — quietly building, up 19.5% overall
watch_today.detail: Google rose 1.48% last session and your position is now up 19.52% overall. No negative news flow. The broader AI theme continues to be a tailwind. Nothing to do here — just a nice green hold.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Sunday session, closing down 0.92% at 8,828. Meanwhile last night in the US it was a different story — the NASDAQ surged 1.91% and the S&P 500 gained 1.08%, both powered by tech optimism. Gold fell 1.2% to $4,172 USD/oz (investors rotating out of the safe haven). Oil barely moved at $76.54. The Aussie dollar is steady at 70.16 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft session today — fell 82 points. Broad-based selling with no single obvious trigger.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Strong session last night — tech and growth stocks led the charge.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Big move last night — best performer of the major indices, lifted by tech enthusiasm.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Essentially flat. US-Iran talks in the background — a deal could push this lower.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back as investors moved into riskier assets like tech stocks.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Barely moved — holding just above 70 cents US.

politics.summary: It's a lean day for Australian political news — only one story made the cut, and it's fairly niche. The broader political calendar is quiet heading into the new week.

stories.title: Law delay bad news for journalism — media regulation reform stalled
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian is reporting that a delay to proposed media law reform is bad news for journalism. The article text isn't available in detail, but the headline suggests legislative changes affecting press regulation or media industry support have been pushed back. For everyday Aussies, this matters if you follow media industry consolidation — delays to reform can leave smaller outlets in a tougher commercial position. We'll keep an eye on this as more details emerge.

ai.summary: The dominant AI theme this weekend is regulation — from the US federal government's hands-off approach clashing with state-level laws, to the G7 debating how to protect kids online from generative AI (AI that creates text, images, and video). There's also a handy consumer deal if you want to try multiple AI tools.

stories.title: Trump tried to block states from regulating AI, but some are forging ahead
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has been trying to stop individual US states from passing their own AI rules, preferring a single federal approach (or no rules at all). But several states are ignoring that and writing their own laws anyway — covering things like AI-generated deepfakes, bias in hiring algorithms, and transparency requirements. For investors in AI-heavy companies like Google and Microsoft, a patchwork of 50 different state regulations would be more expensive to comply with than one federal standard. This tug-of-war is one to watch.

stories.title: J.D. Vance's AI Doctrine
stories.why_it_matters: The Atlantic has published a deep-dive on Vice President JD Vance's approach to AI — essentially a pro-growth, anti-regulation doctrine that wants to keep the US government out of AI development and let the private sector run. The article text isn't available in full, but Vance has been the White House's point person on AI policy. His doctrine matters because it shapes whether US tech giants like Google and Microsoft face guardrails at home, and whether the US pushes that same deregulatory approach globally.

stories.title: Have the G7 effectively regulated generative AI to protect minors?
stories.why_it_matters: Researchers from the University of Sheffield have examined whether the G7 nations (Australia's key trading partners and allies) have done enough to regulate generative AI — the kind that creates realistic text, images, and video — specifically to protect kids online. The article text isn't available in full, but the research context suggests the conclusion is mixed at best. This matters for parents and for investors watching tech regulation risk: tighter rules on AI-generated content would directly affect platforms like YouTube (Google/Alphabet) and social media.

stories.title: Get Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini in a single lifetime AI platform for under $70
stories.why_it_matters: Mashable is spotlighting a deal that bundles access to Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), and Gemini (Google) into a single platform with a one-time lifetime payment under $70 USD. Normally you'd pay $20-30/month per service. For anyone who wants to try the three leading AI assistants without committing to multiple subscriptions, this is a practical, low-cost way to experiment. No article text available for more specifics, but worth checking out if you're curious about AI tools.

sport.summary: Round 16 of the NRL wrapped up this weekend with some big results — the Roosters smashed the Sharks, Melbourne Storm demolished Canberra, and the Gold Coast Titans pulled off a thriller against Penrith. In AFL, Carlton's positional gamble with Nick Crichton is making headlines, and Western Bulldogs coach Luke Beveridge is calling for the national draft to move to October.

stories.title: Titans edge Panthers 19-18 in a thriller at Cbus Super Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Your local Gold Coast Titans pulled off a massive upset at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday, beating the back-to-back premiers Penrith Panthers 19-18. It doesn't get much tighter than that — a one-point win at home against one of the toughest teams in the comp. Big result for the Titans' season.

stories.title: Roosters outclass Sharks 27-8; Warriors and Storm also salute
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters were dominant on Sunday night, thumping the Sharks 27-8 at Allianz Stadium. James Teddy reportedly copped a brutal knock during the match — his availability for next week will be worth watching. Meanwhile Melbourne Storm put on a show against Canberra, winning 42-20, and the Warriors beat the Cowboys 38-20 in Auckland.

stories.title: Bulldogs reveal why Nick Crichton has been moved from edge to centre
stories.why_it_matters: The Canterbury Bulldogs have explained why they've made the surprising call to move star edge forward Nick Crichton to centre — a big positional shift that has raised eyebrows. The article text isn't available in full, but the ABC piece digs into the coaching logic behind the move. Bulldogs fans will want to read this one — it could reshape how Canterbury's backline functions for the rest of the season.

stories.title: Carlton's huge Fraser call and the trio redefining the ruck role in AFL
stories.why_it_matters: AFL.com.au is reporting on a significant selection call from Carlton — a major decision around Tom Fraser — and examining three players who are changing how the ruck role is played in modern footy. The full article text isn't available, but the piece appears to be a tactical deep-dive heading into the mid-season period. Carlton fans and footy analytics enthusiasts will find this worth clicking.

stories.title: Luke Beveridge calls on AFL to move national draft to October
stories.why_it_matters: Western Bulldogs coach Luke Beveridge is publicly pushing the AFL to move the national draft from its current November slot to October, saying 'it just makes sense'. An earlier draft would give clubs more time to integrate new players into pre-season programs and fill list spots sooner. It's a governance debate that's been simmering for years — whether the AFL acts on it this year remains to be seen, but Beveridge putting it on the record publicly adds pressure.
